# Backed By Fans custom renderer kit

Use this kit to create and test an onchain membership renderer, show its representative artwork to
the creator, and prepare deployment through the creator's browser wallet.

Canonical environment

- Robinhood testnet, chain ID 46630, is the only public renderer chain for this version.
- A renderer is shared directly as its same-chain contract address. There is no renderer registry,
  submission flow, catalog, crosschain lookup, or platform enablement step.
- Robinhood mainnet is out of scope.

Public renderer contract

- Implement the exact BackedByFans.MembershipRenderer.v1 Solidity interface and membership types.
- Required methods are rendererSchema, rendererName, engineCount, engineName,
  validateConfiguration, previewSVG, previewTokenURI, and renderTokenURI.
- previewSVG returns a complete SVG document. previewTokenURI and renderTokenURI return complete
  metadata data URIs with a displayable image.
- Use the canonical Solidity files and generated Foundry artifact ABI. The package writer embeds the
  generated ABI; do not write or maintain another ABI by hand.
- Rendering is read-only. It must not alter membership ownership, payments, rewards, referrals,
  expiration accounting, or creator payout identity.

Media behavior

- PreviewContext.nativeMedia carries temporary browser-processed JPEG or PNG bytes immediately
  before a read-only preview call. It is not part of the renderer package and must not be sent to
  the loopback helper or stored by the platform.
- Production renderTokenURI receives MediaConfig. A renderer may read the configured onchain media
  store, use that media, produce generated-only art, or fail clearly when media is unsupported.
- A renderer may crop, filter, recolor, transform, mask, combine, reinterpret, or ignore media.
  Validity is based on the displayed result and creator approval, not proof that source bytes or
  appearance were preserved.

Authoring and local evidence

1. Start from the bundled Foundry renderer template and preserve Solidity 0.8.36, Cancun, and the
   enabled optimizer profile.
2. Add focused Forge tests for deterministic complete output, active and expired states,
   generated-only behavior, nativeMedia behavior, onchain MediaConfig behavior, and clear failures.
3. Run Forge locally without a production key.
4. Run scripts/build-package.ts against the final Foundry project. It builds the contract, embeds
   the generated artifact ABI, measures runtime and complete final initcode including constructor
   arguments, checks raw salt || initcode against Robinhood Nitro's limit, and computes the CREATE2
   address.
5. Run scripts/render-gallery.ts on the package. Inspect all six local examples: token IDs 1, 7,
   and 42; active and expired; generated and image-slot cases.

Browser visual approval

- Hand the same renderer package to the public renderer page. Prefer the optional
  scripts/session-helper.ts loopback handoff; use drag-and-drop or file selection when loopback is
  denied, expired, or unavailable.
- Import and preview require no account, SIWE, OAuth, connected wallet, hosted relay, session
  database, or persistent media storage.
- Browser examples use the canonical RPC and the same public renderer input as memberships.
  Browser-selected media stays in memory and may be included in ordinary read-only RPC calldata.
- Show every representative output or failure. The creator must approve the exact candidate,
  request set, and results. Any candidate, request, salt, or deployment-input change clears
  approval.

Deployment boundary

- Local Anvil success does not prove Robinhood Nitro will admit a public transaction. Measure the
  complete final payload and let the browser independently recheck the package, canonical CREATE2
  deployer, unoccupied predicted address, and Nitro envelope.
- Do not deploy with an agent-held key, cast send, backend signer, exported key, mnemonic, password,
  or generated secret file.
- After approval, show Robinhood testnet, the final payload size, salt, and predicted address. Only
  after the creator clicks Deploy may wagmi/viem simulate and pass its exact request to the creator's
  browser wallet.
- Report success only after wagmi/viem supplies a successful receipt and code is visible at the
  predicted address. Normal completion should say the chain and copyable renderer address without
  requiring receipt, verification, journal, or code-proof expertise.
- Deploying the new direct-renderer protocol is separate from deploying a creator renderer. After
  local validation, stop for explicit operator approval; the operator enters the encrypted
  deployment password interactively. Never request or record that password.
